study type: Descriptive study of trends (retrospective database analysis)
outcome: Timing of TXA administration relative to delivery
Differences in TXA timing by mode of delivery
Prevalence of medical comorbidities in TXA recipients
cohort: The study included 1,544,712 deliveries occurring at greater than 24 weeks' gestation in the United States between January 1, 2016, and February 21, 2023, identified from the Cerner Real-World Database.
finding: Tranexamic acid is most commonly administered after delivery, but a significant number of patients are receiving it prior to delivery in the United States without clear evidence to guide optimal timing.
mod_finding: A total of 80.4% of patients who received TXA before delivery had a cesarean delivery, indicating a strong association between antenatal TXA use and cesarean section.
cross-section timing: Data collected from January 1, 2016, to February 21, 2023
gest_age: Deliveries occurring at greater than 24 weeks' gestation; majority of patients who received TXA delivered between 37 and 41(6/7) weeks (81.4%).
